nf3tstatue:guide-text:
Statues

Carve a person in stone, or cast one in metal.

Making a stone statue
Craft a statue block from stone bricks of one rock: a small statue block from four (2x2), a large one from nine (3x3), or a bust (just the head) from two in a row. Polished marble makes marble statues. Place the block, hold a chisel in your hand and a hammer in your off hand, and rightmouse the block to open the carving dialog.

Sizes
A small statue is about one block tall and a bust is a head on a pedestal. A large statue fills an area of 3x3 blocks and is four blocks tall (the statue itself is about three and a half), like the Tobias statue, standing on a wide plinth. Its block is drawn as a big block of stone of that size. Place it in the middle of the area; every other block of the area must be free. The finished statue stands where the block was, and breaking any part of it breaks it all.

The dialog
The statue type at the top is Player by default. Choose the player (who is online), the pose (an emote, standing or riding) and the frame of the animation; Best frame picks the most expressive one. Switch the layers on or off: hair, face and beard, then clothing, then armor. Remove the pedestal (off by default) makes the statue stand directly on the ground, with no stone pedestal or platform. Each hand can hold a copy of an item from one of your hotbar slots; nothing is taken from you. With an elk, pick cow or bull, its own pose and frame, and its bridle, face mask, saddle and saddlebags. Copy from a nearby elk lists the loaded elk around you (use Refresh to look again); picking one fills in cow or bull, its antlers and its tack. A bull's antlers can also be set by hand, from none to the biggest. The < and > buttons turn the statue, with the compass direction shown; the second pair only turns the preview.

Committing
Press Commit and the block becomes the finished statue. The chisel and hammer wear down, and the statue can never be carved again. It keeps its design when broken and placed again.

Copying a design
Copy design from lists the finished statues in your hotbar. Picking one fills in the whole dialog, which you can commit as it is or change first. The statue is not used up. Some statues are special statues with a fixed shape and no pose; copying one switches the dialog to that statue type and greys out the player settings. Choose Player in the statue type list to go back, or copy another statue to take its type.

Metal statues
Metal is cast, not chiseled, in a clay mold made around a finished stone statue.

Making the mold. You need fire clay, which stands up to molten metal where ordinary clay would crack. Place a finished stone statue and rightmouse it with fire clay in your hand, one piece at a time. The clay is packed around the statue and rises with every piece, until the statue is buried: eight pieces for a small statue, sixteen for a large one and five for a bust. Then rightmouse the covered statue with an empty hand to lift off the statue mold. The mold remembers the statue's design, and the statue itself is left unharmed, ready to be used again. The mold needs no firing: the heat of the metal hardens it.

Casting. Place the mold on solid ground (hold sneak while placing it). A small statue or bust mold is a block of clay with a hole in the top; a large statue mold fills a 3x3 area and is four blocks tall, so the whole area must be free, and the hole is in the middle block. Pour molten metal into the hole, for example from a crucible, aiming at the middle block of a large mold (bust 300 units, small 600, large 1800): the metal rises in the hole until the mold is full. Let it cool, then break the mold with a pickaxe or your hand to get the metal statue, which has the same design as the stone one. Each mold breaks in the process, so every cast needs a new mold.
